configuration_port_proof.limits: Timer and reply words are fixtures. Local MP5 ports are not host addresses. Raw read primitive existence proves no host route, selected rail, valid electrical range or applied-setting readback.

register_target_proof.limits: Pinned original selector instructions; register read/write replies and status are fixtures. No installer, diagnostics, hardware or host firmware executes. Candidate addresses and bit aliases do not establish physical identities or a usable setting interface.

provider_gate_proof.interpretation: The fixture signature 0x00b40f40 with EBX[31:28]=0 passes A and rejects B. Entry eligibility is not proof of protocol installation, PM binding or device effect.

command_slot_binding_proof.limits: Original instruction slices on synthetic fuses/registers. Compact command encodings differ from fixed PM storage slots; SMT target stride 32 differs from the published CPUID CCD stride 16. Neither equality in some fixtures nor a reachable consumer authenticates a runtime PM/APIC/OS binding. No target machine is available.

map_acquisition_proof.limits: The checked provider query and selected SMN read implementation run on synthetic protocol/descriptor/peripheral inputs. map_inputs_proof.limits: Original instructions execute on explicit synthetic SMU-local words and register replies. No host address alias, native acquisition route, physical target or OS identity is authenticated.

supplemental_local_research.limitation: Selected original instruction slices with explicit fixture boundaries, not full Windows application execution or runtime physical binding. The configuration-transfer review excludes MP1 10h as a getter: it imports the entire block. Baseline contents, DMA completion, and a safe public retrieval route remain unverified.

external_reference_sources.scope: PPR 57896 revision 3.00 page 31: nominal REFCLK 100 MHz. Does not bind the MP5 timer or prove physical clock identities.
Taken branches, sequential loop-end handling, integer SAR/SRC and SEXT semantics, and LSI/SSI translate_ldsti raw register transfers. Not a complete AMD FPU or peripheral model.
SEXT immediate decode adds 7 to the raw four-bit field; translate_sext extracts signbit+1 bits. This is an ISA semantic reference, not a hardware measurement.
Xtensa ISA summary MOVI.N RI7 encoding and asymmetric -32..95 immediate range. URL reference only; no downloaded-document hash is asserted.

prior_local_replay_batch: All 33 existing proof outputs remain unchanged; nine new proofs are checked separately. All 42 current local outputs equal the cloud outputs. No physical hardware execution is claimed.
limitations: The direct word-269 proof uses opaque 32-bit FR loads/stores after an initial Linux replay failure caused by host signalling-NaN conversion. LSI/SSI are not integer load/store instructions; this isolated transfer model does not emulate NaN arithmetic, exception flags or a complete firmware FPU.

Common fields 259..262 are averaged configuration values at fixed firmware-target positions; absent targets can retain old source values that still accumulate. The target-presence mask is not exported with these four values. Field 269 is a direct local configuration mirror, not an average or measurement. Equal-code retention is established for the 0x32220 step-setter path, not every writer. All five physical units remain unverified.

Compact command remap positions and fixed PM storage slots are different coordinate systems. The 64-word command table is built from synthetic presence/core/SMT inputs; its target stride is not the published CPUID CCD stride. Neither matching sample tuples nor reachable consumers establish PM, APIC, physical CCD or OS core identity.

SVI command mirrors can originate from startup local-controller status bits and later software requests. The one-word local status reader performs no device register read packet, freshness check or completion-bit polling. A guarded register writer is replayed with synthetic services; its enabled host route, device effects and independent second-rail setter/readback remain unverified.

MP5 integer multiply/divide helpers, low-then-high timer loads, inclusive deadline comparisons and low32 delay truncation run as original-byte bounded replays. Zero-duration polling disables the deadline. Timer latching, physical Hz, counter events and argument units remain unverified; no additional core/CCD physical unit is assigned.

Twenty DPM fields contain sample shares and software clock/voltage policies. MHz uses the nominal 100 MHz arithmetic, not measured BCLK; physical clock identities remain candidates. State numbers do not identify CCDs/cores or prove selection. Voltage policies do not bind a physical rail or provide device readback. Invalid states count only in the sample denominator; shares are not elapsed-time residency.

SMU enqueue can be inhibited or skipped at pending >= 2. The MP5 update handler writes completion 1 before attempting to queue its dispatcher and does not inspect the queue result. These selected gates do not establish a fixed model-update period, energy-MSR alias, physical unit or freshness guarantee; queue/interrupt services and timing remain fixtures.

GUI/CLI reference APOB/OS comparison requires the published Model 44h SMT2 topology and actual redundant type-3 boundary. An APIC-set match is not runtime provider, record origin, physical identity or PM-slot validation. Original-byte oracles use synthetic APOB and services.

The fixture signature 0x00b40f40 with CPUID 80000001 EBX high nibble zero passes provider A entry eligibility and rejects B in 16,636 synthetic gate replays. No host CPUID, installer or firmware service executes; entry eligibility does not establish runtime protocol installation, register effects, physical mapping or PM binding.

Provider A derives register addresses from group stored IDs; B uses subgroup stored IDs. Both use the first core flag prefix and a core ordinal for bit selection. Address/bit aliases and unchecked original thread indexing prevent treating these as a physical/PM/OS map. Product diagnostics only use flags 0/1 and never select a provider or issue register access.

Local MP5 configuration writes wait for raw timer ticks without polling device completion. The raw-byte reader has no verified host route or write/read pairing. An alternate transition can change the code while retaining the old PM float. Scripted MMIO and timers do not verify electrical effects or units.

The public 9950X3D CPUID capture is from X670E-E BIOS 2904, not the target Creator. Original-byte APIC enumeration with these CPUID replies retains synthetic APOB and services. A matching APIC set is not a runtime provider, PM-slot or physical-core binding.

Shared voltage request at PM index 19 is averaged software volts, not a second-rail readback. Full finite CEIL/clamp path and channel-0 packet route use synthetic responses. The request can differ from the command mirror; device effects and physical rail identity remain unverified.

The APIC affinity consumer runs the sorter, provider getters and constructor together. Fabric/configuration/proximity services are fixtures; enumeration ordinals reach the constructor, not the stored IDs. Synthetic duplicate APICs with missing type 3 do not prove real BIOS failure or a PM/OS binding.

APOB cached HOB lookup and container selection have 502 additional synthetic instruction replays. HMAC, UEFI initialization and diagnostics are not executed. Full-container import validates every record before selecting a unique topology.

APOB protocol enumeration/translation and ordinal ordering are replayed on synthetic records. Dynamic entry points use explicitly recorded REA native analysis seeds. The installer and record producer do not execute. Slot +0x48 has a separate replay with scripted register services; no device access occurs. Runtime provider selection and physical/PM/OS identity binding remain unverified.

The pinned UEFI APIC constructor is replayed against synthetic CPUID. Missing type 3 leaves a zero shift and can produce coordinate collisions; its input coordinates are not bound to firmware PM slots or physical cores.

RSMU 72 broadcasts two threshold alternatives through MP5 75 to present targets. Host reply does not check a success code and MP5 acknowledgement precedes policy selection. This is not independent rail addressing or device readback.
MP5 core row 0 and CCD rows 0/1 reach SMU composite a38c; the adjacent feedback selection uses a distinct a390 stream. A nearby power-limit consumer does not establish a physical unit.

Granite 98.84.0 Fmax read/set and stored policy readback are exposed in GUI and CLI after identity, version and capability checks. Policy helper/fuse/transport inputs remain synthetic; this is not target hardware acceptance or an operating-clock measurement.
Static discovery is not a proof that every function has been recovered; only byte-checked slices are used.

Twelve SVI telemetry fields, three software command mirrors, thirteen core and six CCD rows have static unit evidence. Two additional core rows and one CCD row have an averaged integer-code representation, with unresolved meanings. SVI values can be stale or zero in scale mode 0; neither channel identity nor applied settings are authenticated. Voltage model is not measured rail voltage; conditional sensors may retain old values; counter fractions/percentages have unverified event identities and freshness; CCD row 11 has a late firmware multiply by 100. Core rows 9/10 are averaged GHz request policy values, not measured clocks or independent setting readback. Core row 3 and CCD row 5 are GHz frequency models; CCD row 10 is a GHz fused frequency policy, not measured frequency or setting readback. CCD row 9 is a quantized percentage with zero-denominator retention and no clamp to 100. Other units and physical identities remain unresolved.

Eight remaining row producers now have byte-checked arithmetic and configuration evidence. They still have no verified physical units; timer domains, model coefficient scales and absolute quantities remain unresolved.
Descriptor preparation, submission and source coordinates are checked. MP5-local addresses are not host physical addresses or unit evidence; DMA/completion and interrupts are not emulated.

Exponential/power helper arithmetic, caller compositions and configuration quantization are checked with synthetic coefficients and explicit reciprocal results; calibration and physical units remain unresolved.
Firmware two-slot IDs [0,1] do not establish CPUID CCD/APIC or physical core/OS CPU association. One-slot native mapping remains ambiguous.

61h remains a shared-floor path. Separate override/release commands 11h/12h and 13h/14h select firmware channels 1/2, but do not establish physical rail identity, electrical range, device-side effects or independent setting readback. Software command mirrors are not measurements.
Reciprocal accuracy, floating exception behavior, peripheral effects and live error semantics were not emulated. Packet encodings and polling are checked only against scripted responses.
Synthetic replay does not establish live timing, freshness, atomicity or target-machine acceptance. ASUS 2503 is a reference, not the installed BIOS.
